steps.title: Read it as it is written
steps.body:
Indonesian uses the Latin alphabet and every letter sounds the same every time.

• c is always English ch: campur, cantik, kucing.
• A final k, p or t is swallowed into a glottal stop: tidak, anak, tutup, sakit.
• h is light but present: rumah, sudah.
• j is English j: saja, anjing.
• y always comes with a vowel: saya, ayo, kayu.

steps.title: Two letters, one sound
steps.body:
• ng is the ng of English sing, with no hard g: tangan, dengan, pisang.
• ngg has the hard g: tunggu (wait), tinggal (live).
• ny is the soft n of canyon: nyanyi.
• kh is a plain h: khusus, terakhir.
• sy is sh: masyarakat.
• au sounds like ow in cow: mau (want), jauh (far).
• ai sounds like eye: pantai (beach), pakai (use), sampai (until).

steps.title: Stress and speed
steps.body:
There is no fixed stress. Spread it evenly over the syllables; Balinese speakers lean on the last one. Speak clearly and do not be shy.

If someone talks too fast, say pelan-pelan (slower).

steps.prompt: How does the c in kucing sound?
steps.explain: c is always ch in Indonesian

steps.prompt: The final k in tidak is…
steps.explain: final k, p, t are cut off in the throat

steps.prompt: Which word has the soft ng of English 'sing' (no hard g)?
steps.explain: ngg = hard g; a single ng = sing

steps.title: Selamat
steps.body:
selamat means safe or blessed. Put it before a word and you get a greeting or a wish.

selamat datang – welcome (datang = arrive)
selamat makan – enjoy your meal (makan = eat)
selamat tidur – good night, sleep well (tidur = sleep)
selamat jalan – have a good trip, said to the one leaving (jalan = walk, go)
selamat ulang tahun – happy birthday

steps.title: Four parts of the day
steps.body:
pagi – morning, about 4 to 10
siang – midday, 10 to 15
sore – afternoon, 15 until dark (about 19)
malam – evening and night, after dark

selamat pagi / siang / sore / malam = good morning / day / afternoon / evening.

steps.title: Three ways to say please
steps.body:
tolong – asking for help or a favour: Tolong, minta bil. (Please, the bill.)
mohon – a formal request: Mohon ditunggu. (Please wait.)
silakan – inviting or offering, not asking: Silakan masuk. (Please come in.)

Also useful: permisi = excuse me, minta = ask for. Permisi, minta bil is the friendliest way to ask for the bill.

steps.prompt: It is 8 in the morning. You greet someone with…
A friend is leaving on a trip. You say…
steps.explain: jalan = go; selamat jalan is for the one leaving
silakan offers or invites; tolong and mohon ask

steps.text: ___, minta bil. (Excuse me, the bill please.)

steps.title: Orang
steps.body:
orang = person. Doubling a noun makes it plural: orang-orang = people (often written orang2; the 2 is not a count).

orang + a country = a nationality: orang Indonesia (Indonesian), orang Amerika (American), orang Rusia (Russian).

Fun fact: orangutan is orang + hutan, person of the forest.

steps.title: How to address people
steps.body:
Ibu / Bu – a woman who is older or respected (also: mother)
Pak / Bapak – a man who is older or respected (also: father)
Mbak – a young woman
Mas – a young man (Javanese); Bli – a young man (Balinese)
Kak / Kakak – anyone young, man or woman. The safe universal choice.

steps.title: Family
steps.body:
keluarga – family · orang tua – parents
ibu – mother · bapak, ayah – father
kakak – older sibling · adik – younger sibling
laki-laki – male · perempuan – female
kakak laki-laki – older brother · adik perempuan – younger sister
suami – husband · istri – wife
anak – child · anak laki-laki – son · anak perempuan – daughter
nenek – grandmother · kakek – grandfather
teman – friend · saudara – relative, cousin

steps.title: Pronouns
steps.body:
saya – I (polite) · aku – I (casual)
kamu – you (casual) · Anda – you (formal)
dia – he / she · mereka – they
kami – we (not including you) · kita – we (all of us, including you)
kalian – you (plural)

The same word is also the possessive: saya = I and my, dia = he and his. Position tells you which (next lesson).

steps.prompt: A respected older woman is addressed as…
The safe, universal way to address a young person is…
We, including the person you are talking to:
steps.explain: kita includes the listener; kami does not

steps.title: The thing comes first
steps.body:
Indonesian puts the noun first and the describer after it. English says big house; Indonesian says rumah besar (house big).

rumah besar – a big house
toko kecil – a small shop
kantor pos – post office
nasi goreng – fried rice
air minum – drinking water.

steps.title: I and my are the same word
steps.body:
saya is both I and my; dia is both he/she and his/her. Position decides: before the noun it is the subject, after the noun it is the owner.

teman saya – my friend
saya teman – (wrong: "I friend")
teman ibu saya – my mother's friend
motor dia – her scooter
saya tunggu teman saya – I wait for my friend

A phrase and a sentence differ only by where the describer sits: kafe kecil mereka… (their small cafe…) vs Kafe mereka kecil. (Their cafe is small.)

steps.title: Words for this lesson
steps.body: besar – big · kecil – small · cantik – beautiful · baru – new · bagus – great · suka – like · mau – want · tunggu – wait · tinggal – live · tahu – know · sudah – already · nama – name · toko – shop · kantor – office · mobil – car · motor – scooter · pantai – beach.

steps.explain: the owner comes after the noun

steps.prompt: Which is the complete sentence "Their cafe is small."?
Type: our house (we, not including you)

steps.title: Punya – to own
steps.body:
punya is for anything a person can own.

Saya punya rumah / teman / suami / anak. – I have a house / a friend / a husband / a child.
Kami punya mobil besar. – We have a big car.
Dia tidak punya kakak. – She has no older sibling.
Saya tidak punya waktu. – I have no time.

tidak goes right before punya.

steps.title: Ada – to exist, to be somewhere
steps.body:
ada says that something exists or is located somewhere.

Ada menu? – Is there a menu?
Ada kopi? – Is there coffee?
Tidak ada listrik / air. – There is no electricity / water.
Di rumah saya ada banyak buku. – In my house there are many books.

Compare:
Ibu ada di rumah. – Mum is at home (location).
Ibu ada rumah. – Mum has a house (ada replacing punya).

Ada kelapa? – Maaf, tidak ada. (Is there coconut? – Sorry, none.)

steps.title: Words for this lesson
steps.body: uang – money · waktu – time · kucing – cat · anjing – dog · kopi – coffee · listrik – electricity · air – water · banyak – many · buku – book · kamar – room · kosong – empty · kabar – news · maaf – sorry.

steps.text: Dia tidak ___ kakak. (She has no older sibling.)

options: Do you want coconut? – No thanks.
Is the coconut good? – Sorry, no.
Where is the coconut? – I don't know.

steps.prompt: They have a house in Bali.

lessons.title: First conversation
lessons.subtitle: 28 phrases that get you through the day

steps.title: Meeting someone
steps.body:
Siapa nama? – What's your name? → Nama saya … – My name is …
Berapa umur? – How old are you? → Umur saya … 
Dari mana? – Where are you from? → Dari Rusia.
Asli dari mana? – Where are you originally from?
Tinggal di mana? – Where do you live? → Saya tinggal di Canggu.
Bisa bahasa Indonesia? – Do you speak Indonesian? → Ya, bisa sedikit. – Yes, a little. / Sedikit saja. – Just a little.

saja (just, only) and sekali (very) always go after the word: sedikit saja, mahal sekali, pintar sekali.

steps.title: Getting by
steps.body:
Berapa harganya? / Berapa ini? – How much is it?
Mahal sekali! – Very expensive!
Minta diskon? – Can I get a discount? (minta air, minta tisu – may I have water, tissues)
Bisa bantu? – Can you help?
Maaf, saya tidak bisa. – Sorry, I can't.
Permisi! – Excuse me!
Tunggu sebentar. – Wait a moment.
Saya tidak mengerti. – I don't understand. Bisa pelan-pelan? – Slower, please?
Saya mau pesan. – I want to order.
Bayar di mana? – Where do I pay?

steps.title: Small talk
steps.body:
Apa kabar? – How are you? → Baik. / Bagus. – Good. / Great.
Sudah makan? – Have you eaten? Mau makan? – Want to eat?
Mau ke mana? – Where are you going? → Jalan-jalan. – Just walking around.
Suka di Bali? – Do you like Bali?
Hati-hati di jalan! – Take care on the road!
Saya belajar bahasa Indonesia. – I'm learning Indonesian.
Terima kasih. – Thank you. → Sama-sama. – You're welcome.
Sampai jumpa! – See you!

options: Where are you going? – Just walking around.
Where do you live? – On the street.
What do you want? – A walk.
How do you go? – On foot.

steps.title: Ini and itu
steps.body:
ini = this (near), itu = that (far).

At the start, it is the subject "this is …":
Ini meja. – This is a table.
Ini anak teman saya. – This is my friend's child.
Ini tempat bagus. – This is a great place.

After a noun, it points at that specific one:
meja ini – this table
Saya suka tempat ini. – I like this place.
Cewek ini cantik. – This girl is beautiful.
Saya mau mobil itu. – I want that car.

steps.title: 0 to 10
steps.body: 0 – nol (or kosong) · 1 – satu · 2 – dua · 3 – tiga · 4 – empat · 5 – lima · 6 – enam · 7 – tujuh · 8 – delapan · 9 – sembilan · 10 – sepuluh.

steps.title: Bigger numbers
steps.body:
belas = -teen (11–19): sebelas 11, dua belas 12, tiga belas 13 …
puluh = tens: dua puluh 20, tiga puluh 30 … dua puluh lima 25
ratus = hundreds: seratus 100, dua ratus 200
ribu = thousands: seribu 1,000, lima ribu 5,000
juta = millions: sejuta / satu juta, dua juta

se- means one: sebelas, sepuluh, seratus, seribu, sejuta.
seratus lima puluh ribu = 150,000 (a typical price).

options: This is the book I like.

steps.text: I want that car. → Saya mau mobil ___.

steps.title: Apa – what, which
steps.body:
At the start, apa (or apakah) just marks a yes/no question:
Apakah kamu mau makan? / Apa kamu mau makan? – Do you want to eat?

To ask "what" or "which", apa goes after the verb or noun:
Kamu mau makan apa? – What do you want to eat?
Mau minum teh apa? – Which tea do you want?
Ini mobil apa? – What car is this?

Don't mix up apa and ada: Ada lagi? – Is there more? vs Apa lagi? – What else?

examples.en: What do you want to eat?

steps.title: Siapa – who, whose
steps.body:
"Who" → siapa goes first:
Siapa orang ini? – Who is this person?
Siapa nama kamu? – What is your name? (literally: who is your name)

"Whose" → siapa goes after the noun:
Ini kucing siapa? – Whose cat is this? → Ini kucing saya.
Ini kunci siapa? – Whose keys are these? → Ini kunci teman saya.
Ini mobil siapa? – Whose car is this? → Ini mobil orang tua.

steps.title: Words for this lesson
steps.body: kunci – keys · tempat – place · meja – table · teh – tea · hijau – green · makan – eat · minum – drink · lagi – more, again · kotor – dirty · buah – fruit.

steps.prompt: What do you want to eat?
steps.explain: apa goes after the verb when asking "what"

options: What do you want to eat?

steps.title: Three prepositions
steps.body:
di – at / in / on, nothing moves: di rumah, di pantai, di Bali
ke – to, movement towards: ke rumah, ke pantai, ke Bali
dari – from, origin (also time): dari rumah, dari Bali, dari jam 8

Kamu tinggal di mana? – di Bali.
Kamu mau ke mana? – ke toko.
Kamu datang dari mana? – dari Amerika.

Near / far: di sini – here, di sana – there · ke sini – (to) here, ke sana – (to) there · dari sini – from here, dari sana – from there.

steps.title: Verbs of movement
steps.body:
datang – come, arrive
pergi – go (pergi ke Ubud; needs ke when a place follows)
pulang – go home (also said when leaving)
jalan – walk; jalan-jalan – go for a stroll; jalan – street
kembali – come back; uang kembali – change (money); terima kasih kembali – you're welcome
sampai – reach, arrive at

dengan = sama – with. sekarang – now. menit – minute.

options: From here to there is 15 minutes.

steps.title: Tidak vs bukan
steps.body:
tidak – no / not, before verbs, adjectives and ada:
Saya tidak mau. – I don't want.
Ini tidak mahal. – This isn't expensive.
Tidak ada waktu. – There's no time.
Casual speech: nggak (Nggak mau. – Don't want.)

bukan – not, before nouns and pronouns:
Dia bukan teman saya. – He is not my friend.
Ibu saya bukan dokter. – My mum is not a doctor.
Ini bukan rumah kami. – This is not our house.

steps.title: Belum and jangan
steps.body:
belum – not yet. Use it whenever "yet" fits, even if you never plan to:
Sudah makan? – Belum. (Eaten yet? – Not yet.)
Saya belum tahu. – I don't know yet.
Mereka belum punya anak. – They don't have children yet.

jangan – don't (command):
Jangan lupa! – Don't forget!
Jangan masuk. – Don't come in.
Jangan ke sana. – Don't go there.

bisa – can (ability) vs boleh – may (permission):
Boleh saya pakai ini? – May I use this?
Tidak boleh parkir di sini. – No parking here.
Saya tidak bisa. – I can't.

steps.title: Words for this lesson
steps.body: dokter – doctor · mahal – expensive · murah – cheap · lupa – forget · masuk – enter · parkir – park · pakai – use, wear · tahu – know · anak – child · ambil – take.

steps.text: Dia ___ teman saya. (He is not my friend.)

options: You can't park here, it's full.

steps.text: ___ saya pakai ini? (May I use this?)

steps.title: Part 1 – moving here
steps.body:
Selamat pagi, teman-teman! Saya datang di Bali 2 tahun yang lalu. Sebelum itu saya tinggal di Moskow, kota besar di Rusia. Saya datang ke sini dengan pacar saya. Sekarang kami tinggal di Canggu, dekat pantai.

yang lalu – ago · sebelum itu – before that · kota – city · dengan (= sama) – with · pacar – boyfriend/girlfriend · sekarang – now · dekat – near.

steps.title: Part 2 – the house
steps.body:
Rumah kami tidak besar, tapi bagus. Ada dua kamar tidur, satu kamar mandi, dapur dan ruang tamu. Saya tidak tinggal sendiri – pacar saya, satu kucing dan banyak teman sering datang.

tapi – but · kamar tidur – bedroom · kamar mandi – bathroom · dapur – kitchen · ruang tamu – living room · sendiri – alone · sering – often.

steps.title: Part 3 – daily life
steps.body:
Saya suka Bali karena orangnya ramah dan tempatnya tidak sepi. Di sini ada banyak orang asing dari negara lain. Setiap hari saya main ke pantai, dan pada hari libur kami masak bersama. Pembantu kami baik hati – dia bersihkan rumah setiap hari. Tapi di sini selalu panas!

karena – because · ramah – friendly · sepi – quiet, empty · orang asing – foreigner · negara lain – another country · setiap hari – every day · main – play, hang out · hari libur – day off · masak – cook · bersama – together · pembantu – helper · baik hati – kind · bersihkan – clean · selalu – always · panas – hot.

steps.prompt: Saya datang di Bali 2 tahun yang lalu.
options: I came to Bali two years ago.
I'm coming to Bali in two years.
I've been in Bali for two years.
Two years ago I left Bali.

steps.prompt: Sebelum itu saya tinggal di Moskow.
options: Before that I lived in Moscow.
After that I lived in Moscow.

steps.prompt: Every day I go to the beach.
On days off we cook together.

steps.title: Day, month, year, hour
steps.body:
The unit word goes first, then the value:
hari Rabu – Wednesday (day Wednesday)
bulan Juni – June
tahun 2026 – the year 2026
jam 7 pagi – 7 a.m. (jam first! 7 jam = 7 hours)
tanggal 31 Desember – the 31st of December

Watch out: hari Minggu – Sunday, but minggu – week.

steps.title: Days and months
steps.body:
Senin – Mon · Selasa – Tue · Rabu – Wed · Kamis – Thu · Jumat – Fri · Sabtu – Sat · Minggu – Sun

Januari · Februari · Maret · April · Mei · Juni · Juli · Agustus · September · Oktober · November · Desember

Parts of the day: pagi – morning · siang – midday · sore – afternoon · malam – night.

steps.title: When
steps.body:
hari ini – today · pagi ini – this morning · kemarin – yesterday · besok – tomorrow · sekarang – now · saat ini – at the moment
sebelum – before · sesudah / setelah – after
3 hari lagi – in 3 days (lagi after the amount)
minggu depan – next week · minggu kemarin / minggu lalu – last week · bulan depan – next month · tahun lalu – last year

Saya datang 3 hari lagi. – I'm coming in 3 days.
Kita bertemu hari Sabtu jam 5 sore. – We meet on Saturday at 5 p.m.

steps.explain: hari Minggu = Sunday, minggu alone = week

steps.prompt: We meet on Saturday at 5 p.m.

steps.text: Saya tinggal di sini dari tahun ___. (last year)

steps.title: Question words
steps.body:
kapan – when: Kapan kamu datang? – Besok.
kenapa – why: Kenapa kamu tidak makan? – Karena saya tidak lapar.
untuk apa – what for: Ini untuk apa? – Untuk masak.
berapa – how many / how much, the answer is a number: Berapa orang? – Dua.
bagaimana (casual: gimana) – how: Bagaimana rasanya? – Enak. · Bagaimana kalau besok? – How about tomorrow?
yang mana – which one: Mau yang mana? – Yang ini. / Yang merah. (this one / the red one).

steps.title: Jam berapa vs berapa jam
steps.body:
Word order flips the meaning:
Jam berapa? – What time? → Jam 7. (seven o'clock)
Berapa jam? – How many hours? → 4 jam. (four hours)

Same pattern: Berapa hari? – How many days? · Berapa orang? – How many people? · Berapa harganya? – How much is it?

lapar – hungry · rasanya – the taste · merah – red · kalau – if, how about.

steps.text: ___ kamu tidak makan? – Karena saya tidak lapar.

lessons.title: Verbs and places
lessons.subtitle: the verbs you use every day, where things are

steps.title: Everyday verbs 1
steps.body:
ambil – take · kasih / beri – give · beli – buy · jual – sell · bayar – pay · tanya – ask · cari – look for · coba – try · dapat / terima – get, receive · mulai – start · selesai – finish · habis – run out, finished

Berapa saya harus bayar? – How much do I have to pay?
Bisa bayar pakai kartu? – Can I pay by card?
Boleh saya ambil ini? – May I take this?
Saya cari rumah di Ubud. – I'm looking for a house in Ubud.

steps.title: Everyday verbs 2
steps.body:
pakai – use, wear (pakai baju – wear clothes · tidak pakai gula = tanpa gula – without sugar)
perlu / butuh – need · harus – must · sewa – rent · dengar – hear · lihat – see · masuk – enter · keluar – go out · pesan – order · kirim – send · taruh – put · bilang – say · bawa – bring · bertemu / ketemu – meet · bikin – make

Saya harus pulang. – I have to go home.
Saya perlu uang kecil. – I need small change.
Kopi tanpa gula. – Coffee without sugar.
Bawa ke sini. – Bring it here.

steps.title: Where is it?
steps.body:
di depan – in front · di belakang – behind · di dalam – inside · di luar – outside · di atas – on top, upstairs · di bawah – under, downstairs · di sebelah – next to · di dekat – near
ke kiri – to the left · ke kanan – to the right · lurus / terus – straight on · lewat – via, past

Buku ada di bawah meja. – The book is under the table.
Kunci di dalam tas. – The keys are in the bag.
Toko di sebelah kafe. – The shop is next to the cafe.
Terus, lalu ke kiri. – Straight on, then left.

steps.prompt: How much do I have to pay?

steps.text: Boleh saya ___ ini? (May I take this?)

steps.prompt: The book is under the table.

options: The shop is next to the cafe.
The shop is behind the cafe.
The shop is in the cafe.
The shop is far from the cafe.

steps.title: More and most
steps.body:
lebih + adjective = more: lebih besar – bigger · lebih murah – cheaper
X lebih … daripada Y: Bali lebih panas daripada Moskow. – Bali is hotter than Moscow.
Saya lebih suka teh. – I prefer tea.

paling + adjective, or ter- prefix = most: paling enak – the tastiest · paling murah – cheapest · tercantik – the most beautiful · terbaik – the best.

steps.title: Now, before, later
steps.body:
Verbs never change. Time words do the work.

Now: sedang / lagi – in the middle of: Ibu sedang masak. – Mum is cooking. · Kamu lagi di mana? – Where are you right now?

Past: tadi – earlier today · sudah – already · dulu – back then · pernah – ever / have … before · yang lalu – ago
Tadi pagi saya makan dengan teman. – This morning I ate with a friend.
Dulu saya tinggal di Ubud. – I used to live in Ubud.
Pernah ke Spanyol? – Ya, pernah. (Ever been to Spain? – Yes, I have.)
Saya belum pernah coba durian. – I've never tried durian.

Future: akan – will · nanti – later · besok – tomorrow · minggu depan – next week
Saya akan pergi ke sana. – I will go there.
Nanti saya datang lagi. – I'll come again later.

steps.title: At the market
steps.body:
pedagang – seller · Cari apa? – What are you looking for? · segar – fresh · pisang – banana · alpukat – avocado · semangka – watermelon · anggur – grapes · telor – eggs · keju – cheese · susu – milk · roti – bread · sayuran – vegetables · buah-buahan – fruit · bumbu – spices
cukup – enough · tambah lagi – add more · Berapa semuanya? – How much all together? · gratis – free · uang kecil – small change · lain kali – next time · sangat suka – really like.

steps.prompt: I used to live in Ubud.

options: Ever been to Spain? – Yes, I have.

steps.text: ___ saya datang lagi. (Later I'll come again.)

steps.prompt: This morning I ate with a friend.
